question: For each rating category of the first movie rented by customers—where the first movie is identified based on the earliest payment date per customer—please provide the average total amount spent per customer and the average number of subsequent rentals (calculated as the total number of rentals minus one) for customers whose first rented movie falls into that rating category.
sql:
-- Final aggregation by rating
WITH first_payment_per_customer AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        MIN(payment_date) AS earliest_payment_date
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
first_rental_id_per_customer AS (
    SELECT 
        p.customer_id,
        p.rental_id
    FROM payment p
    JOIN first_payment_per_customer fpc 
        ON p.customer_id = fpc.customer_id 
        AND p.payment_date = fpc.earliest_payment_date
),
first_movie_rating AS (
    SELECT 
        fr.customer_id,
        f.rating
    FROM first_rental_id_per_customer fr
    JOIN rental r ON fr.rental_id = r.rental_id
    JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
),
customer_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        SUM(amount) AS total_amount_spent
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_rental_count AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_rentals
    FROM rental
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT 
    fm.rating,
    ROUND(AVG(ct.total_amount_spent), 2) AS avg_total_amount_spent,
    ROUND(AVG(crc.total_rentals - 1), 2) AS avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM first_movie_rating fm
JOIN customer_totals ct ON fm.customer_id = ct.customer_id
JOIN customer_rental_count crc ON fm.customer_id = crc.customer_id
GROUP BY fm.rating
ORDER BY fm.rating;

How this database is organised (written by an LLM from the tables' notes and keys):
Transaction tables are payment, rental, and inventory, recording financial activity, film loans, and physical stock. Lookup tables include actor, address, category, city, country, customer, film, language, staff, and store, describing entities and their attributes. The film_actor and film_category tables act as junctions linking films to actors and categories. Connections flow as follows: customer links to address and store; staff links to address and store; store links to address and staff. City links to country. Film links to language. Inventory links to film and store. Rental links to customer, inventory, and staff. Payment links to customer, staff, and rental.
